edges.description: Hyperactive PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling drives endothelial proliferation and dysregulated angiogenic/lymphangiogenic sprouting.
Mosaic PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation stimulates soft-tissue and skeletal anabolic growth within the affected limb segment.
Dysregulated angiogenic and lymphangiogenic remodeling produces low-flow capillary, venous, and lymphatic malformations across the extremity.
Cutaneous capillary malformation manifests clinically as nevus flammeus.
Venous malformation and persistent lateral embryonic veins manifest as varicosities.
Malformed lymphatic channels form microcystic and macrocystic lymphatic malformations.
Ectatic, valveless malformed extremity veins impair venous return.
Venous engorgement, lymphatic swelling, and thrombophlebitis cause chronic extremity pain.
Blood stasis and localized consumptive coagulopathy within ectatic venous channels trigger venous thrombosis.
Thrombi formed within ectatic extremity and pelvic venous malformations embolize to the pulmonary arterial tree.
Pelvic and colorectal mucosal venous malformations bleed into the gastrointestinal lumen.
Cutaneous lymphatic stasis and vesicular lymphangiectasia predispose the limb to recurrent bacterial cellulitis.
Regional soft-tissue and bony overgrowth manifests clinically as limb hypertrophy.
Unilateral lower-extremity bony and soft-tissue overgrowth produces leg-length and girth asymmetry.

evidence.snippet: On the basis of these results, we used BYL719 to treat nineteen patients with PROS. The drug improved the disease symptoms in all patients. nodes.description: Post-zygotic somatic gain-of-function missense variants in PIK3CA (encoding the p110alpha catalytic subunit of class IA phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase; predominantly hotspot alleles p.Cys420Arg, p.Glu542Lys, p.Glu545Lys, p.His1047Arg, and p.His1047Leu) arise in embryonic vascular/mesenchymal progenitors at low mosaic allele fractions (often <10% mutant cells) and constitutively elevate baseline lipid kinase activity, converting PtdIns(4,5)P2 to PtdIns(3,4,5)P3.
